purpose: Correct whole-column empirical convection and lower-air subcloud evaporation in independently solved moisture reservoirs. No fitted coefficient, wind change, humidity reset or planetary retune. Conservatively route upper rain re-evaporation into lower air.
physical_definition: Hold all r39 coefficients, shared wind, calibrated total capacity, normalized moist-profile capacity fractions, boundaries, mass/vertical transport, land and actual lower-ocean evaporation, drying, conservative storms and planetary parameters fixed. Preserve old layer rainfall as exact control. In corrected option, local dynamical gate and supersaturation overflow remain layer-specific, but the empirical whole-column convection coefficient is computed once from total W/Ws and applies to both Wi. Thus total convective rain equals its original column relation, including the 0.1mm dry-water numerical floor, rather than the sum of a convex exponential on independently varying layer humidities. Falling non-overflow rain in both layers is attenuated using actual lower-layer RH, representing the air it traverses, with the original subcloud evaporation coefficient. Overflow remains unattenuated. No new physical coefficient; no latent-heat, explicit cloud-plume, ice or vertical-energy claim. Old proportional profile remains equivalent to roundoff. Previous parcel experiment is not coupled in this study. Additionally upper non-overflow rain removes its gross amount from upper vapor; the fraction re-evaporated in lower air is added to actual lower water, not retained aloft. The pair of internal precipitation-transfer terms cancels exactly in the total-column equation. Lower locally formed rain retains its original effective attenuation. Ground rain is the attenuated dynamic/convective total plus unattenuated overflow; both layer equations include the signed precipitation transfer. This routing introduces no water source or fitted parameter. Proportional-profile equivalence refers to total ground rain, not the two individual layer losses.
